name: Local Waypoints Calculator Parity with Cloud API

asi.root_cause: build_geometry includes every waypoint as per-DoF section boundary, forcing v=0 at monotonic pass-throughs per paper §III-B only true local extrema need v=0

description: Switch build_geometry to true local extrema only (paper §III-B). Duration gap 24.65%→9.13%, max_dev 0.265→0.357

asi.hypothesis: Only use true local extrema as per-DoF section boundaries, matching paper §III-B
asi.result: Major duration improvement (9.81→8.59s), but max_dev increased (0.265→0.357) vs cloud's 0.260
asi.next_step: Reduce path deviation while keeping the duration gain - need to improve the tracking/interpolation for monotonic pass-through waypoints

description: Remove pre-alignment, pass initial v/a directly to core. Duration gap 9.13%→4.20%, but max_dev 0.36→0.47

asi.hypothesis: Remove pre-alignment so core handles non-zero initial v/a directly, avoiding 0.71s braking overhead
asi.result: Duration improved 8.59→8.20s (gap 9.13%→4.20%), but deviation worsened (max 0.36→0.47, mean 0.11→0.21)
asi.issue: Non-zero initial velocity/acceleration causes tracking issues - DoFs with initial motion overshoot the reference path more easily
asi.next_step: Fix deviation by improving tracking for DoFs with non-zero initial state, especially near section boundaries

description: Smaller delta_u_ref (0.005) made everything worse - duration 8.86, kinematic fail

asi.hypothesis: Smaller delta_u_ref makes tracking tighter and reduces deviation
asi.result: Worse on all metrics: duration 8.20→8.86, max_dev 0.47→0.43 (slightly better), kinematic FAIL
asi.next_action_hint: Try larger delta_u_ref or different approach to reduce deviation

description: Larger delta_u_ref (0.02) slightly worse duration 8.25 vs 8.20

asi.hypothesis: Larger delta_u_ref gives tracking more room, might reduce oscillation
asi.result: Slightly worse on all metrics, delta_u_ref tuning not the right lever
asi.next_action_hint: Focus on section transition logic and dwell time elimination

description: Set a=m*af_fast at section transitions caused kinematic failure and worse duration

asi.hypothesis: Setting acceleration to m*af_fast at section transitions eliminates dwell time
asi.result: Kinematic FAIL and duration worse (8.62 vs 8.20). The acceleration jump violates jerk limits.
asi.next_action_hint: Need smoother section transition - can't just snap acceleration

description: Fix forward_position_to_s braking overshoot + bounds check: duration gap 4.20%→-0.01% (7.87s vs 7.87s!). Deviation still higher (0.42 vs 0.26).

asi.hypothesis: Fix forward_position_to_s to handle braking overshoot positions, and extend bounds in advance_one_dof
asi.result: Duration gap virtually eliminated (7.87s vs 7.87s). Max deviation 0.42 vs cloud 0.26, mean 0.15 vs cloud 0.11
asi.key_fix: forward_position_to_s was incorrectly mapping overshoot positions to wrong sections, causing s_dt and m calculation errors. Also extended section bounds for braking overshoot.
asi.next_step: Reduce path deviation from 0.42 to closer to cloud's 0.26 while keeping duration parity

description: Smaller sim_dt no help for deviation

asi.hypothesis: Smaller sim_dt (0.001) for finer tracking resolution reduces deviation
asi.next_action_hint: Try structural approach - improve u_ref initialization or add waypoint constraints
asi.result: No improvement in deviation. Tracking quality not limited by discretization.
asi.rollback_reason: No improvement, takes longer to compute

description: All waypoints with bounds fix: duration 9.21s (worse), deviation 0.46 (still bad)

asi.hypothesis: Re-add all waypoints as section boundaries with v=0 to reduce deviation
asi.next_action_hint: Use selective waypoint inclusion or improve tracking quality
asi.result: Duration much worse (9.21 vs 7.87s) and deviation barely improved (0.46 vs 0.42). All-waypoints approach doesn't work even with bounds fixes.

description: Pass-through velocity approach: catastrophic - duration 10.43s, deviation 0.57, kinematic fail

asi.hypothesis: Add pass-through waypoints as section boundaries with non-zero velocity from fast trajectory
asi.next_action_hint: Deviation is structural - caused by DoFs being at different u values near waypoints. Try improving u_ref initialization or tracking to synchronize DoFs at waypoints.
asi.result: Terrible - duration 10.43s, deviation 0.57, kinematic fail. Adding section boundaries with non-zero v breaks the tracking scheme and fast trajectory computation.

description: Best iteration by max_dev: worse duration 8.16, same max_dev

asi.hypothesis: Select best tracking iteration by max_path_deviation instead of avg
asi.next_action_hint: Remove enforce_waypoint_sync since it's not helping. Focus on the u_ref initialization instead.

description: u_ref = min of all DoFs: 16% worse duration, kinematic fail

asi.hypothesis: Initialize u_ref as element-wise min of all DoFs' fast trajectory u values
asi.rollback_reason: Duration 16% worse, kinematic failure. Min-of-all is too conservative.

description: Average u_ref + multi-region update: max_dev 0.331 (best yet!) but duration 8.95 (+13.76%)

asi.hypothesis: Average u_ref reduces max deviation, multi-region update_u_ref helps convergence
asi.result: Average+multi-region: duration 8.95 (13.76%), max_dev 0.331 (much better), kinematic pass. BUT duration regression is primary metric fail.
asi.key_finding: Average u_ref significantly reduces max_dev (0.416->0.331) at cost of 13.76% duration gap. Pure average alone is 22.83%. Multi-region update (top-3) helps convergence vs single-region.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed: duration_gap 13.76% vs current best -0.01%

name: Local Waypoints Calculator - Multi-region Update + Overshoot Clamp

description: Baseline for new segment: delta_u_ref 0.05, duration -0.01% (7.87s), max_dev 0.456

asi.hypothesis: baseline measurement for new segment with delta_u_ref=0.05
asi.focus: need to reduce max_dev from 0.456 to closer to cloud 0.260 without regressing duration

description: Multi-region update_u_ref (top-3): duration 18.69%, kinematic fail. Too aggressive.

asi.hypothesis: Update top-3 non-overlapping violation regions per iteration instead of just one
asi.result: Much worse: duration 9.34 (18.69% gap), kinematic fail. Updating multiple regions destabilizes the tracking.
asi.next_action_hint: Try top-2 or just overshoot-only multi-region. Or try a completely different approach - pre-compensating u_ref for initial velocity overshoot.

description: Probe-and-adjust u_ref for overshoot: duration 4.78%, max_dev 0.456 (same). Just increases duration.

asi.hypothesis: After initial u_ref from slowest DoF, probe track and raise u_ref where any DoF overshoots by > delta
asi.rollback_reason: Duration regressed to 4.78% without reducing deviation
asi.next_action_hint: Raising u_ref always increases duration. Need approach that reduces deviation without changing total time. Try: damped update corrections, or solve intermediate trajectory properly.

description: Baseline: smoothness analysis - duration gap -0.01%, max_dev 0.416 (still 60% higher than cloud)

asi.hypothesis: Work on path smoothness to reduce max_dev from 0.416 to closer to cloud's 0.260
asi.root_cause: DoFs diverge in u-space: DoF with initial wrong-direction velocity overshoots and can't be slowed fast enough due to jerk limits (j_max=10)
asi.key_issue: At worst deviation time, u values spread: dof1=4.32, dof2=5.36, dof3=4.51 (spread=1.04) vs cloud spread=0.45
asi.action: Analyze tracking algorithm to understand why DoF2 gets ahead and how to keep DoFs synchronized
